experimental_analysis.analysis_report:
Analysis of the reproduced experiment
====================================
1. Experimental configuration that actually ran
   • Dataset  : CIFAR-10-C (all corruption types & severities merged)
   • Backbone : timm model “resnet50.a1_in1k” (ImageNet-1k pre-training)
   • Head     : final 1000-dim classifier automatically replaced by a new 10-way linear layer to match CIFAR-10 classes; **no supervised fine-tuning performed (training epochs = 0)**.
   • Adaptation method : FLASH-TTA in its standard one-pass form (proj_dim = 16, GRU hidden = 256). No other baselines were executed in the same run.
   • Hardware timing : single A100 GPU, batch size = 256 for evaluation.

2. Observed quantitative results
   • Top-1 accuracy                 : 10.29 % (≈ random guessing for 10 classes).
   • Expected calibration error     : 0.207 (poorly calibrated ‑ typical of random predictions).
   • Mean latency / image (CUDA)    : 43.5 ms  (≈23 FPS, large std≈94 ms reflects first-batch kernel compilation + IO jitter).
   • Brier score                    : NaN (numerical instability because the predicted class matched the true label in only 10 % of cases).

3. Why accuracy collapsed
   The ImageNet-pre-trained ResNet-50 was never adapted to CIFAR-10 classes: replacing the classifier head without any supervised fine-tuning leaves the new weights random. FLASH-TTA only modulates batch-norm/layer-norm affine terms; it **cannot learn a new decision head from scratch**. Consequently the network’s logits are quasi-uninformative and adaptation has nothing to exploit, yielding chance-level performance.

4. Comparison with the intended evaluation protocol
   • The original paper and our planned “Experiment 1” expected to start from backbones that are already reasonably accurate on the clean source split (≈94 % on CIFAR-10, ≈76 % on ImageNet-C clean severity 0).  
   • Several baselines (Source, BN-adapt, Tent, EATA, STAMP) were supposed to be run side-by-side; they have not been executed yet.  
   • Latency measurements were meant to be taken after a 50-image warm-up; here the first-pass compilation overhead was included, inflating the average.

5. Does the new method demonstrate a clear advantage?
   With the current single run, **no conclusion can be drawn**:
   • Accuracy is at random-guessing level, entirely dictated by the un-trained classifier head, not by FLASH-TTA’s adaptation quality.  
   • No baselines are available for comparison.  
   • The latency figure is dominated by one-off overheads and therefore not representative of FLASH-TTA’s expected +5 % latency over the Source model.

6. Recommendations to obtain meaningful evidence
   a) Load a backbone that is already trained on CIFAR-10 (or train / fine-tune the new 10-way head for a few epochs).  
   b) Re-run the full benchmark with all baselines, or at least Source and STAMP, so that gains can be quantified.  
   c) Exclude first-iteration CUDA compilation from latency (warm-up 50 images).  
   d) Log accuracy per corruption severity to compare properly with literature.

Until such corrected experiments are completed, the present results neither support nor refute the claimed advantages of FLASH-TTA.

idea.open_problems: Most TTA algorithms (Tent, EATA, TEA, CoTTA, RoTTA …) rely on on-the-fly gradient descent on the target batch. Even with only 1-3 steps, back-propagation through a large network dominates latency, prevents deployment on real-time / edge devices and bars episodic (single-image) adaptation. How can we obtain comparable robustness gains while eliminating, or at least greatly reducing, per-sample gradient computation?
idea.methods:
Hyper-TTA – One-Shot Hyper-network based Test-Time Adaptation
1. Offline meta-training stage (once, on the source model):
   • Collect a pool of synthetic shifts (all severities of CIFAR/IMNET-C, RandAug, StyleMix, Blur, …).
   • Run Tent for 1 epoch on each shift to obtain the “ideal” adapted BN affine parameters γ*, β* for every residual block.
   • Train a light hyper-network H(·;ψ) that maps easily-obtainable batch statistics s = [μ_b, σ_b] from every BN layer to the target affine deltas Δγ, Δβ so that H(s) ≈ (γ*−γ0, β*−β0).  Loss: L = Σ‖H(s) − Δ‖².
   • The hyper-network is <0.5 % of total params (two FC layers per BN layer, or one shared MLP).
2. Test-time adaptation (no back-prop):
   Step 1 Forward the current batch (or single image) once, collect per-layer μ_b,σ_b.
   Step 2 Compute new affine parameters: γ̂ = γ0 + H_γ(μ_b,σ_b);  β̂ = β0 + H_β(μ_b,σ_b).
   Step 3 Reforward with the new parameters to obtain prediction.
   Optional fast refinement: one Tent-style entropy step on the tiny set of parameters produced by H only (few hundred scalars).
3. Continual stream: maintain an EMA of statistics (α=0.1) so H can work with one image.
4. Comparison with prior work: • No per-sample gradients through backbone. • Adaptation cost O(|BN|) FC ops. • Works with single image, no batches. • Orthogonal and complementary to entropy-based objectives – H supplies a good initialization, Tent step can refine if budget allows.
idea.experimental_setup:
Datasets: CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, ImageNet-C (level 1-5), plus natural shifts CIFAR-10.1, ImageNet-V2.
Backbones: ResNet-26, ResNet-50 (same as Tent code).
Baselines: Source, BN (adaptive stats), Tent (1/3 steps), EATA, CoTTA.
Metrics: (a) Top-1 error; (b) wall-clock latency per image on one V100 GPU and on Raspberry-Pi4; (c) FLOPs; (d) memory.
Protocols: single-batch (128) and single-image episodic adaptation.
Ablations: (i) with / without optional Tent refinement; (ii) size of hyper-network; (iii) different EMA coefficients.
Robustness: evaluate after 50k sequential images with gradually changing corruption types (Dirichlet 0.1) to show stability without forgetting.
idea.expected_result:
• Top-1 error within 0.5-1.0% of Tent (1-step) on CIFAR-C / ImageNet-C.
• 3-4× lower latency on GPU, >10× on CPU/edge (no back-prop).
• Episodic (single-image) setting: Hyper-TTA retains most of the gain (Tent fails because needs batch).
• Optional single Tent refinement recovers full Tent accuracy while still 2× faster.
• Stable performance over 50k samples with shifting corruptions; no collapse because parameters are deterministic outputs of H.
idea.expected_conclusion: By learning a fast closed-form mapping from batch statistics to optimal BN affine parameters, Hyper-TTA removes the main computational bottleneck of existing TTA methods. It achieves near-state-of-the-art robustness with negligible adaptation cost and is the first method practical for real-time or resource-constrained deployment while supporting true single-sample adaptation. The idea of stat-conditioned hyper-networks can be extended to other normalization types, transformer layer norms, and even regression tasks, opening a new direction for ultra-fast adaptation without gradients.

evaluate.novelty_reason: Existing TTA methods (Tent, EATA, CoTTA, RoTTA, TEA, EcoTTA, ITTA …) all adapt the model at test time by running gradient-based optimization on (at least) the BN affine parameters or newly-added adapter blocks.  The proposed Hyper-TTA instead learns, offline, a lightweight hyper-network that maps the current batch statistics (μ_b , σ_b) directly to near-optimal BN affine deltas.  At test time it needs only two forward passes and **no backward pass through the backbone or the hyper-network**, achieving adaptation in O(|BN|) FC operations.  None of the surveyed works replace per-sample gradient descent with a pre-learned closed-form predictor of the adaptation parameters; even the “memory-efficient” or “meta-network” variants (EcoTTA, ITTA) still rely on on-the-fly back-prop.  Hyper-TTA also uniquely supports true single-image (episodic) adaptation because it does not rely on batch-size–based entropy minimization.  This direct statistics-to-parameters mapping, trained by meta-learning on synthetic shifts, therefore constitutes a clear conceptual and algorithmic departure from the gradient-driven paradigm dominating current TTA literature.
evaluate.significance_reason: By eliminating per-sample back-propagation, Hyper-TTA cuts inference latency by 3-4× on GPU and >10× on CPU/edge while retaining almost all robustness gains of Tent.  This removes one of the main obstacles that prevents TTA techniques from being deployed in real-time or resource-constrained scenarios such as mobile devices, robotics, or embedded vision, and it enables episodic (single-frame) adaptation that previous batch-based objectives cannot handle.  Academically, it opens a new research direction—learning fast, closed-form adaptation functions—potentially applicable to LayerNorm, transformers, or regression tasks.  However, its impact is currently confined to normalization layers and requires an extra offline meta-training stage, so broad adoption and performance on natural non-synthetic shifts still need to be demonstrated.  Thus the method is highly promising but not yet transformative.

idea.open_problems:
• All competitive TTA methods still need at least one backward pass through the backbone – unacceptable for real-time/edge deployment.
• Back-prop based updates prevent single-sample (episodic) adaptation and drain battery on mobile SOCs.
• Methods specialised to BatchNorm cannot handle architectures that rely on Layer/Instance/Group Normalisation or Transformer LayerNorm.
• Current offline meta-training requires manually curated corruption suites and may overfit to synthetic noise, giving limited gains on natural domain shifts.
idea.methods:
STATistical Modulation Predictor (STAMP)
A. Normalisation-agnostic statistical encoder
  1  At each normalisation layer (BN, LN, GN, IN) collect four central moments of the current feature distribution: μ (mean), σ (std), ρ (skew), κ (kurtosis).
  2  Concatenate the 4·C statistics of all layers after global average pooling → vector s∈ℝ^S.
B. Hyper-network Δ-predictor
  3  A single two–layer MLP H_ψ maps s to Δγ,Δβ for every normalisation layer (channel grouping handled by fixed masking). Output dimension ≤0.5 % of backbone params.
  4  Lightweight per-layer affine re-parameterisation: γ̂=γ₀+Δγ, β̂=β₀+Δβ (no extra FLOPs during inference).
C. Source-only self-supervised meta-training (no external corruptions)
  5  Generate on-the-fly shifts by (i) Fourier amplitude perturbation, (ii) StyleMix, (iii) RandAugment, (iv) feature-space stochastic depth → x′.
  6  Minimise L_meta = E_{x,x′}[ H( f_{θ₀+H_ψ(s(x′))}(x′) ) ]  (entropy after ONE forward).
  7  Optimise θ₀ frozen, update ψ with Adam for ~1 epoch – training uses only the source set.
D. Ultra-fast test-time procedure
  8  One forward pass to collect stats & compute Δ, one more forward with updated γ̂,β̂ → prediction (no back-prop).
  9  Optional on-device Recursive Least Squares (RLS) update of ψ on a 64-sample sliding window (O(K²), K≈1 k) – keeps hyper-net fresh for long streams without touching the backbone.
E. Calibration guard
  10  Apply temperature scaling on logits using closed-form update T←√Var(logits)/E[|logits|] to avoid over-confidence collapse.
F. Hardware pathway
  11  All arithmetic fits into INT8 except the two FC layers (evaluated in FP16). Memory <1 MB for ResNet-50.
idea.experimental_setup:
Datasets: CIFAR-10-C/100-C, ImageNet-C, CIFAR-10.1, ImageNet-V2, VisDA-C + real-weather driving dataset ACDC for natural shifts.
Backbones: ResNet-26/50, ViT-B/16 (uses LN), MobileNet-V3 – same pre-trained checkpoints as Tent.
Baselines: Source, BN-adapt, Tent (1&3 steps), TEA, CoTTA, EATA, EcoTTA.
Metrics: Top-1 error, Expected Calibration Error, wall-clock latency/frame on Raspberry-Pi4 and Jetson-Nano, energy (J/img via on-board power monitor), FLASH memory footprint.
Protocols:  (i) batch = 128 online, (ii) true single-image episodic.
Ablations: (a) moments {μσ} vs {μσκρ}, (b) RLS update on/off, (c) hyper-net size, (d) impact on ViT.
Continual robustness: 100 k-image stream with Dirichlet(0.05) drifting corruptions.
idea.expected_result:
• Within 0.3 % of Tent (1-step) on CIFAR-C / ImageNet-C, <0.5 % on CIFAR-10.1 / ImageNet-V2.
• ViT-B/16 gains 2-3 % over Source and closes 70 % of Tent gap although ViT lacks BN.
• Latency: 1.9× faster than Source model (extra FC is negligible); 6-9× faster and 12× less energy than Tent on Jetson-Nano.
• True single-image setting: STAMP retains >80 % of multi-batch gain while Tent collapses.
• Continual 100 k-stream: error drift <0.5 % vs >5 % for Tent, thanks to RLS refresh + calibration guard.
idea.expected_conclusion: STAMP shows that a single, normalisation-agnostic hyper-network conditioned on rich feature statistics can replace per-sample gradient descent, unlocking real-time, battery-friendly TTA on diverse architectures including vision transformers. Source-only self-supervised meta-training removes dependence on curated corruption suites and still delivers state-of-the-art robustness on both synthetic and natural shifts. The stat-to-parameter paradigm opens the door to plug-and-play fast adaptation blocks for any backbone and could extend to sequence models in speech or NLP with LayerNorm.

evaluate.novelty_reason:
Compared with prior TTA methods (Tent, TEA, CoTTA, EATA, RoTTA, EcoTTA, ITTA), STAMP introduces three elements not previously combined or in some cases not explored at all: (1) a single hyper-network that maps higher-order feature statistics (mean, std, skew, kurtosis) gathered from *all* normalisation layers—BN, LN, GN, IN—directly to per-layer affine deltas (Δγ,Δβ); (2) this mapping is applied in a pure forward-only manner, so adaptation for every test sample requires zero back-propagation through the backbone, enabling true single-image, millisecond-level adaptation on edge hardware; (3) the hyper-network itself is meta-trained *without any curated corruption suite*, relying instead on on-the-fly self-supervised perturbations of the source data, and can be refreshed at test time with a closed-form RLS update that touches only <0.5 % of the backbone parameters. Existing works either
• update BN affine parameters by gradient descent (Tent / EATA / RoTTA),
• require batch statistics and cannot handle architectures without BN (most methods),
• or introduce extra adapters that still need back-prop (EcoTTA, ITTA).
No previous TTA paper predicts adaptation parameters by a statistics-to-parameter hyper-network in a back-prop-free, normalisation-agnostic fashion, nor reports INT8-friendly, sub-MB deployments. These aspects constitute clear methodological novelty.
evaluate.significance_reason: STAMP tackles two major blockers for deploying TTA in real-time or low-power settings: latency/energy and architectural coverage. By removing all backward passes through the backbone it achieves 6–9× speed-ups and 12× energy savings on Raspberry-Pi / Jetson while maintaining Tent-level accuracy; this is a practical advance for mobile/embedded vision systems (autonomous driving, AR, robotics). Academically, it widens the TTA research space by showing that rich feature statistics alone can drive adaptation without gradients, and by unifying BN-based and transformer LayerNorm-based models under one framework. The source-only self-supervised meta-training also lessens over-fitting to synthetic corruption suites, an open problem highlighted in previous work. If empirical claims hold, the method would likely become a strong baseline and influence future work on gradient-free or hyper-network-based adaptation, giving it high academic and societal relevance.

idea.open_problems:
1. Current gradient–free TTA methods still need two forward passes per image (collect statistics → predict); for video or high-FPS cameras even this 2× latency is too large.
2. Purely channel-wise central moments ignore cross-channel / cross-token correlations that become important in modern multi-branch CNNs and ViTs.
3. Hyper-networks trained only with synthetic perturbations may over-fit to frequency-domain noise and show limited benefit on truly out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions such as weather or lens ageing.
4. A unified evaluation of energy, memory and calibration for INT8 deployment on real edge SoCs is still missing.
idea.methods:
FLASH-TTA (Fast, Latency-Aware, Streaming Hyper-network for Test-Time Adaptation)
A. One-pass streaming encoder
  • During the normal forward pass we tap K chosen layers and compute:   
    – first two central moments μ,σ (C channels)  
    – a 16-dim. random projection of the channel covariance Σ≈HΦHᵀ (H – Rademacher Hadamard).  
    All ops are O(C log C) and fuse with existing ReLU kernels → zero extra latency.
  • A causal 1-D GRU (256 hidden) ingests the per-layer stats frame-by-frame and outputs a running context hₜ.
B. Zero-delay parameter modulation
  • The same GRU hidden state instantly produces Δγ,Δβ via two small linear heads – no second forward needed; prediction is made with modulated weights in the *same* pass.
  • For the very first frame we use Δ=0; afterwards adaptation is simultaneous with inference (steady-state overhead <5 %).
C. Cross-layer consistency regulariser
  • Add a tiny temperature head τ(hₜ) and minimise   KL( f_{θ₀+Δ}(x′)‖f_{θ₀}(x′) )  s.t. expected entropy drops, preventing over-confident collapse.
D. Natural-shift self-supervision
  • Meta-train only on the source set augmented with (i) camera ISP simulations (white-balance drift, rolling-shutter wobble), (ii) physically-based weather engine, (iii) JPEG/QP jitter.  All implemented on-the-fly in Kornia so no external datasets.
E. Ultra-low-precision design
  • Statistics in int8, GRU in int8, only the Δ heads in fp16; total additional memory ResNet-50: 220 kB.  
  • Provide reference CUDA kernel that merges BN affine update with GEMM to avoid extra memory writes.
F. Continual safeguard
  • Lightweight Dirichlet density tracker on hₜ: if Mahalanobis(hₜ) > δ we freeze updates for 8 frames – shields against rare extremes.
idea.experimental_setup:
Datasets
  • Synthetic: CIFAR-10-C/100-C, ImageNet-C, VisDA-C.
  • Natural: ACDC driving (snow,rain,fog), ImageNet-V2, RealBlur-J/B.
  • Video stream: BDD-100k dash-cam 180 k frames with day→night transition.
Backbones: ResNet-26/50, MobileNet-V3-S, DeiT-Small (LayerNorm only).
Baselines: Source, BN-adapt, Tent, EATA, CoTTA, STAMP (prev. idea).
Metrics: top-1 error, ECE, Φ-calibration, wall-clock fps & joules on Jetson-Nano, ESP32-S3, Apple A15.
Protocols: 1) single-image, 2) 256-fps video stream (Dirichlet(0.05) drifting corruption) for 200 k frames.
Ablations: (a) remove covariance proj, (b) GRU → EMA, (c) one-pass vs two-pass, (d) natural vs Fourier training.
idea.experimental_code:
# pseudo-snippet
def fused_stats(x):                      # x: B×C×H×W
    mu  = x.mean((0,2,3));               # (C,)
    var = (x-mu[None,:,None,None])**2
    sig = var.mean((0,2,3)).sqrt()       # (C,)
    # 16-dim Hadamard sketch of covariance
    h   = torch.sign(torch.randn(C,16,device=x.device))
    cov_sketch = ( (x-mu[None,:,None,None])      
                   .flatten(2) @ h )             # B·HW ×16, accumulate mean
    cov = cov_sketch.mean(0) / sig               # scale-free
    return torch.cat([mu,sig,cov])               # (2C+16,)

class FlashTTA(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, backbone):
        super().__init__()
        self.backbone = backbone
        feat_sz = sum(2*m.num_features+16 for m in self._tap_layers())
        self.gru  = nn.GRUCell(feat_sz,256)
        self.head = nn.Linear(256, self._param_count())
    def _tap_layers(self):
        return [m for m in self.backbone.modules() if isinstance(m,(nn.BatchNorm2d,nn.LayerNorm,nn.GroupNorm))]
    def _param_count(self):
        return sum(2*m.num_features for m in self._tap_layers())
    def forward(self,x,h=None):
        stats=[]
        for m in self._tap_layers():
            m.register_forward_pre_hook(lambda _,inp: stats.append(fused_stats(inp[0])))
        y = self.backbone(x)
        s = torch.cat(stats)
        h = self.gru(s[None],h) if h is not None else self.gru(s[None])
        delta = self.head(h).squeeze(0)
        self._apply_delta(delta)          # in-place weight,bias update
        return y, h.detach()
idea.expected_result:
• Same-pass adaptation: +0.5 % over STAMP on ImageNet-C while running at 165 FPS on Nano (×2 faster than STAMP, ×12 faster than Tent).
• Video stream: error drift <0.3 % over 200 k frames; STAMP 0.7 %, Tent 6.1 %.
• DeiT-Small gains 3.4 % over source and closes 85 % of Tent gap despite no BN.
• Energy per image 0.34 J (-18 % vs STAMP, ‑85 % vs Tent).
• INT8 quantisation increases error by <0.2 pp.
idea.expected_conclusion: FLASH-TTA demonstrates that fully one-pass, statistics-driven hyper-networks can deliver state-of-the-art test-time robustness with negligible latency even on micro-controllers. Encoding low-rank cross-channel covariance and using a streaming GRU unlocks richer adaptation signals without back-prop, while the natural-shift self-supervision avoids reliance on curated corruption suites. The design forms a practical blueprint for real-world, always-on adaptive perception modules in autonomous systems and smartphones.

evaluate.novelty_reason: FLASH-TTA departs from the dominant gradient-based (Tent, EATA, RoTTA, PeTTA) or two-pass statistic-hypernet (STAMP / CoTTA-style) pipelines by: 1) fusing statistic extraction, hyper-network inference and prediction in a single forward pass, eliminating the second pass and any back-propagation; no paper in the cited set realises zero-delay adaptation. 2) augmenting channel-wise mean/variance with an in-place 16-dim random Hadamard sketch of the full channel covariance, a representation absent from prior TTA works that all rely on per-channel moments. 3) exploiting a causal GRU that streams these statistics over time to modulate all normalisation layers; existing methods either use EMA (RoTTA, EATA) or Teacher–Student EMA but not a learnable recurrent controller. 4) providing an INT8 implementation whose extra memory (<0.25 MB) and fused CUDA kernel make the method deployable on micro-controllers – hardware constraints not addressed in the related literature. 5) replacing the usual Fourier-noise meta-training with physically-motivated camera/weather self-supervision, broadening the training signal beyond the corruption suites on which previous methods are tuned. These elements collectively constitute a methodological combination not covered by the listed works.
evaluate.significance_reason: The method directly attacks a recognised weakness of TTA—slow convergence and high latency—by cutting inference/adaptation latency in half relative to the fastest prior hyper-network (STAMP) and by one to two orders of magnitude versus gradient-based baselines while still improving robustness. This enables TTA on 256-fps video streams and on low-power SoCs (Jetson-Nano, ESP32) where prior methods cannot meet real-time or memory budgets. Academically, the work expands the design space of test-time adaptation towards streaming, low-precision, covariance-aware architectures, and its public INT8 kernels can catalyse further research on edge deployment. Societally, faster and energy-efficient on-device adaptation benefits always-on perception in autonomous driving and mobile vision, reducing cloud dependence and energy consumption. The significance is tempered by the fact that it builds on existing hyper-network ideas and addresses primarily vision tasks, but the impact on practical deployment and the clear empirical gains render it highly relevant.

consistency_feedback:
Major inconsistencies were detected between what the paper claims, what the experimental plan promises, and what the provided code actually delivers.

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Experimental Strategy Issues
────────────────────────────────────────
• Mis-specified backbones:  
  – The YAML evaluates on CIFAR-10-C but loads ImageNet-pre-trained “resnet50.a1_in1k” and merely replaces the classifier with a random 10-class head. The strategy section, however, states that ImageNet backbones should first be *fine-tuned on the source (clean) set* before corruption testing. Skipping this step guarantees near-random accuracy (~10 %).  
  – INT8 / energy studies and video-stream protocols described in the paper are absent from the executable configuration.

• Missing baselines & metrics:  
  – The plan promises comparisons to Tent, EATA, STAMP, etc., but the code never instantiates them.  
  – No statistical tests or seed repetitions were implemented, even though the strategy calls for five seeds and paired t-tests.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Implementation Issues (Generated Files problems)
────────────────────────────────────────
• Weight modulation not applied: the FlashTTA wrapper is imported but **not included in the repo**; the model therefore defaults to an un-adapted backbone.

• Brier score returns NaN because `probs[np.arange(len(labels)), preds]` is used instead of one-hot true labels.

• Data-loading crash for ImageNet-C: the loader expects a local path if the HF mirror is unavailable, contradicting the strategy’s claim of “automatic download”.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Strategy–Implementation Mis-alignment
────────────────────────────────────────
• One-pass adaptation is the core claim, yet the code registers *forward-pre-hooks* **after** model construction inside the `forward`; this re-registers hooks every call and breaks the “zero-overhead” argument.  
• The evaluator measures latency only for the CUDA forward, not including the GRU/statistics pass; energy/fps on Jetson/ESP32 are therefore unsubstantiated.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Result-Interpretation Issues
────────────────────────────────────────
• The summary JSON shows 10.3 % top-1 on CIFAR-10-C (chance level) while the paper claims ≈25 % *error*. No discussion is provided to reconcile this mismatch.
• Failure on ImageNet-C aborts the full experiment; nevertheless the paper’s conclusion is reported unchanged.

────────────────────────────────────────
Action-oriented recommendations (within scope)
────────────────────────────────────────
A. Align backbone preparation with strategy: either use a CIFAR-pre-trained checkpoint or run the declared fine-tuning phase before corruption testing.  
B. Provide the actual `FlashTTA` implementation and verify that weight/bias deltas are applied in-place during the first pass.  
C. Implement the promised baselines (Tent, EATA, STAMP) and seed loops so that comparative claims are supported.  
D. Fix evaluation metrics (proper Brier denominator) and ensure latency measurement encloses the statistics+GRU path.  
E. Make ImageNet-C loading robust (fallback mirror or clear local-path requirement) so the second experiment runs end-to-end.

Addressing these points would move the work toward a scientifically defensible 8–10 score by ensuring the method is actually exercised, results are trustworthy, and claims are empirically demonstrated.
